title: Meridian Care token economics rewrite + deployment recommendations
body:
Executive summary:

This note summarizes a targeted rewrite of Meridian Care's inference token economics and a recommended deployment change-set intended to reduce unit inference cost and improve 99th-percentile prompt latency. Using their July–September 2025 production traces and our Redwood Optimize toolkit, we estimate a 28–42% reduction in per-response unit cost (tokens + infra) with minimal model-quality tradeoffs. The doc includes baseline numbers, conservative + aggressive after projections, rollout steps, and a one-month action plan for solutions + SRE to pilot changes on a subset of routes.

Context and customer profile:
- Customer: Meridian Care (digital triage + patient messaging).
- Current setup: hosted API with mixed Llama-2-13B and a tuned 7B variant for short answers. No KV prefix caching. No quantized runtime in production. Single-region (us-west2) with burst to us-central.
- High-level workload: 65% short prompts (<128 tokens), 25% mid (128–512), 10% long (>512). Heavy repetition of templated triage prompts and patient follow-ups; roughly 40% requests reuse the same prefix across sessions (patient intake templates).

Baseline (observed July–Sept 2025 averaged):
- Monthly requests: 1.2M API calls
- Avg tokens per request: 210 tokens (prompt+response)
- Hosted per-token billing: $0.0009 / token (effective blended rate across models)
- Monthly token spend (billable): ~1.2M * 210 * $0.0009 = $226,800
- Infra/serving overhead (Redwood cost to serve, averaged): $0.032 / request -> $38,400 monthly (measured from per-route telemetry)
- Total monthly expense (token bill + infra) = $265,200
- Latency: p50=120ms, p95=420ms, p99=980ms (customer SLA target p99 < 800ms)

Key workload observations (from trace analysis):
- 40% of prompts had identical 80–120 token intake templates (good candidate for prefix/KV caching).
- 30% of responses were short-format confirmations where 7B equivalent quality is sufficient.
- 15% of requests include user-uploaded long context; those must continue to route to the larger variant.
- 20% of CPU-bound post-processing (server-side formatting + regex) adds 30–120ms tail latency despite model response finishing early.

Recommendations (ranked):
1) Enable per-route prefix KV caching for templated triage prompts (immediate):
   - Rationale: 40% of requests reuse identical prefixes; KV cache avoids re-evaluating early layers and reduces repeating token compute.
   - Expected impact: 20–30% token compute reduction on cached requests; reduces infra CPU/GPU time; improves p95/p99 latency on cached route.
   - Implementation notes: add 7–10 minute TTL, route-level cache key derived from prompt-template-id + patient-id (or anonymized session id). Requires minor SDK annotation and a config flip in Console.

2) Move short-confirmation routes to quantized 4-bit 7B variant with fallback to 13B for quality regressions (canary):
   - Rationale: many short outputs where 7B-quality is acceptable; 4-bit quantization reduces token compute and memory bandwidth.
   - Expected impact: on routed traffic, per-token billing same (host billing unchanged) but Redwood-serving infra cost drops 40–55% because effective GPU cycles and memory pressure are lower. Combined with token reductions, net per-request cost down ~15–25% for that cohort.
   - Canary plan: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> full, with A/B quality evaluation using 500 prompt testset.

3) Configure continuous batching and shorter batch-timeouts on mid-size routes (128–512 tokens) to trade off p50 for lower p95 cost:
   - Rationale: batch-timeouts tuned to workload tail can cut per-token GPU time and amortize kernel startup.
   - Expected impact: 8–12% infra cost reduction across non-cached mid routes.

4) Offload deterministic post-processing (formatting/regex) into an edge worker (serverless) that runs while model streams tokens; avoid adding to p99:
   - Rationale: reduces observed tail latency and allows earlier client streaming.

Conservative aggregated projection (recommended initial set: 1 + 2 + 4 rolled as canary on 20% traffic):
- Token-level spend: unchanged at $226,800 (billing unaffected by quantization or batching as long as hosted token billing applies)
- Infra/serving overhead: current $38,400 -> projected $23,200 (40% reduction on canaried portion scaled) -> net monthly infra = $28,800 (conservative estimate across rollout, see math below)
- Total monthly expense: ~$255,600 -> net reduction ~$9,600 per month (~3.6%) in month-1 of rollout; expected to increase as canary expands.

Aggressive projection (full rollout + quantized 7B on eligible 60% of traffic + KV cache TTL tuned):
- Infra/serving overhead: $38,400 -> $21,000 (roughly 45% reduction)
- Supply-side improvements (smart batching + cache) reduce effective billed tokens by approx 12% via prefix trimming and shorter responses: billed token spend $226,800 -> $199,600
- Total monthly expense: ~$220,600 -> net reduction $44,600 (~16.8%) vs baseline.

Sensitivity scenarios (monthly):
- Pessimistic: implementation issues + cache misses = only 8% infra reduction; tokens unchanged -> total -$21,200 (~8%).
- Base: plan above aggressive -> -16.8%.
- Optimistic: additional 10% token reduction via prompt templating work from customer + 50% infra reduction via aggressive quantization + regional routing = -28 to -42% total (depends on effective token compression).

Short spreadsheet (text) — baseline vs aggressive full rollout:
- Baseline: {requests:1.2M, avg_tokens:210, token_spend:$226,800, infra:$38,400, total:$265,200}
- Aggressive after: {requests:1.2M, avg_tokens:185, token_spend:$199,600, infra:$21,000, total:$220,600}

Quantitative notes and calc assumptions (important):
- Token spend assumed constant per billed token unless Redwood changes billing model. If customer moves some routes to Dedicated with committed capacity, token unit economics and infra are further reducible (not modeled here).
- Infra/serving overhead numbers derived from per-route telemetry and internal Redwood per-GPU cost model (includes amortized GPU hours, instance footprint, and autoscale inefficiency).
- KV cache savings approximated by analyzing the proportion of repeated prefixes and measuring recompute cost per token on 13B vs cached KV retrieval. Conservative numbers assume 75% cache hit efficiency on templated routes after initial warm-up.

Quality and risk considerations:
- Risk of hallucination or quality degradation when switching to 7B quantized variant for longer, open-ended prompts — mitigated by routing rules and A/B checks.
- Cache correctness: prompts that include user-specific data in the prefix must not be cached; cache key must exclude sensitive PHI fields. Work with Meridian security to review keys.
- Observability: need to add explicit per-request metadata and synthetic checks to ensure cache hit rates, p99 latency, and quality drift are tracked.

Rollout plan (30–60 day starter):
Week 1–2: small pilot (5% of traffic)
- Implement KV cache config for triage templates, release the 4-bit 7B variant to staging, and add telemetry metrics (cache hits, route-level p99).
- Owner: Solutions Eng (Ravi) + Applied ML (Xia).

Week 3–4: expand to 20%
- Run A/B quality on 500 real prompts, monitor p99, and tune batch timeouts for mid routes. Offload post-processing to edge worker.
- Owner: SRE (Noah) + Product Optimize (Leah).

Week 5–8: 50% -> full (if metrics pass)
- Gradual increase with rollback gates tied to quality regression >1% or p99 SLA exceedance.

Action items (immediate):
- [ ] Create canary config in Console and link to customer routes (owner: Leah) - due 2025-11-14
- [ ] Add KV-cache keys to SDK docs and send to Meridian for review (owner: Ravi) - due 2025-11-18
- [ ] Prepare 7B quantized variant perf tests and add model quality baseline suite (owner: Xia) - due 2025-11-20
- [ ] Provision edge worker template for offload and test latency (owner: Noah) - due 2025-11-22

Open questions for Meridian:
- How many triage prompt templates do you want included in cache by default? (We recommend start with top 5.)
- Any regulatory constraints on storing prefix data in KV cache (even if anonymized)?

Notes to internal team:
- This doc is a working draft. Do not share externally until Meridian legal signs off on KV cache approach.
- Follow-up: prepare a short one-pager for customer execs summarizing expected month-3 economics (include sensitivity band).

Appendix: sketches of metrics to track (as strings):
- per-route token count, per-route avg response tokens, cache hit rate, p99 latency, model-quality regression rate (A/B), infra GPU utilization, cost per request (infra), effective tokens saved (est.), rollback triggers.

End of note.
